candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication allergy and contraindication screening
candidate.educational_objective: Before administering sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, identify documented hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides as a contraindication and clarify the prescription rather than attempting dose reduction or premedication.

options.A: Administer the prescribed dose because a prior hypersensitivity reaction does not affect later use of the same medication.
options.B: Administer a reduced first dose because lowering the dose removes the contraindication from prior hypersensitivity.
options.C: Premedicate with an antihistamine and administer the medication because premedication overrides the labeled contraindication.
options.D: Do not administer the medication and clarify the prescription because known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides is a contraindication.

candidate.rationale: The current sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim label lists known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides as a contraindication. D is therefore the best nursing action before administration. A ignores the documented contraindication. B is not supported by the label; dose reduction does not remove a hypersensitivity contraindication. C is also unsupported because antihistamine premedication does not negate the labeled contraindication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides; serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis can occur.
